### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**15** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b09fc767ad4a6cd8af1022e8a1044cd703f876ce` — the merge of head `4200bbebc7fa86bc43e9e93422cbfaeb134c34d9` into base `55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b09fc767ad4a6cd8af1022e8a1044cd703f876ce && git checkout b09fc767ad4a6cd8af1022e8a1044cd703f876ce
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c 4200bbebc7fa86bc43e9e93422cbfaeb134c34d9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c && git merge --no-ff 4200bbebc7fa86bc43e9e93422cbfaeb134c34d9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55337f4ce35dbe62434b23517547a0b5052b936c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

security#1 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4200bbebc7fa86bc43e9e93422cbfaeb134c34d9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/visitor-verification-resend.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/signup-existing-address-success-shape.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/verification-email-failure-propagation.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/run-after-response.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-actor-guards.ts (`resolveActor`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (`isEmailDeliveryLive`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/send-verification-email.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts (the shadowing resend route), better-auth 1.7.12 `dist/api/dispatch.mjs`, `dist/api/routes/session.mjs`, `dist/api/routes/email-verification.mjs`, `dist/plugins/bearer/index.mjs`, ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/VerifyEmailPromptPage.tsx, scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs, .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml

Inputs: the PR body, its file list, the net diff against the merge base `a52761fdd7`, the check-runs on the head, and the ruling (maintainer, 2026-11-04, option G). The committed tree touches no published schema and no governed path; the PR body and both changesets declare `Clause-②: no` with no arm, so the tree itself decides no review face. This record is the at-tier review the seat ordered for a security-channel fix, and the scope above is every path of the diff outside the prose faces plus the code those hunks cite.

Check-runs on the head: every check is completed; none is still running. All are green except `Check Changeset` (two runs, both failure). Its only annotation is the foreign-changeset refusal on `.changeset/sign-up-mail-after-response.md`, the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class the gate's own header names. Red by design: the gate's header says the check stays red either way; the workflow that runs it (`pr-automation.yml`) triggers on `pull_request` only, never `merge_group`; the check is not a required context. The third red-by-design condition, a PR comment naming the gate and the cause, is still owed: the body names it, a comment does not yet.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The rule under a live transport holds.** `sendAfterResponseOnSignUpAndVisitorResend` hands the visitor's resend to `sendAfterResponseOnPublicDoor`, whose deferral is keyed on the `Request` the call carries, so the visitor's send runs after the response and its failure reaches `logAfterResponseSendFailure` only. Read in better-auth's resend route: for a caller it finds no session for, an address with no account or an already-confirmed one never reaches the send callback (a token is minted locally), and the remaining address reaches it; with the send deferred, every one of the three answers `200 { status: true }` behind the route's own floor. Correct, and ablation leg 1 (two timeouts) pins exactly this.
2. **The rule under a non-live transport holds.** `refuseVisitorResendWithoutLiveTransport` runs in `globalBeforeHook` ahead of the endpoint, is keyed on the endpoint's declared path and the presence of a `Request`, reads `isEmailDeliveryLive` once, and refuses every caller `resolveActor` finds no user for with one coded body, `400 EMAIL_SERVICE_REQUIRED`, before any address is read. Correct. The code is the one plugin-auth already answers on `/change-email` and in the identity import for the same deployment condition; it is typed against the ADR-0112 ledger (`RegisteredErrorCode`), so no ledger change.
3. **The signed-in resend stays honest.** A caller `resolveActor` resolves passes the before-hook; inside the endpoint the route resolves the session and records it on the endpoint context, so `isVisitorResendInEndpointContext` reads a session and the callback is awaited as before. ⑦'s renamed case and ⑧'s cookie-and-bearer case pin it. Correct.
4. **The discriminator: can the two readers disagree in a way that splits answers by address? No.** Measured in better-auth 1.7.12: the bearer plugin's before-hook returns its cookie as a context patch, and `dispatchAuthEndpoint` merges every before-hook's patch into the request headers only after `runBeforeHooks` has returned, so a bearer caller reads as no session to `getSessionFromCtx` inside our before-hook; `resolveActor` reads the bearer header itself (unsigned token against the session store) and is the right reader there. Ablation leg 3 pins it. The two readers can still disagree in one direction, a credential the store knows but whose signature the endpoint does not accept: the before-hook then passes and the endpoint reads a visitor, and the callback decides how the send runs, so every address still gets the same `200`. In the other direction (before-hook reads no caller, endpoint reads a session) the refusal is address-independent by construction. Neither direction produces an answer that depends on the address. The cached `context.session` the before-hook's read leaves behind is `null` for a visitor, which the endpoint's reader treats as unread and re-reads, so no stale reading crosses from the hook into the endpoint.
5. **A server-side `auth.api` call with no `Request` is neither deferred nor refused — right.** The ruling is about the visitor on the public door; a call with no `Request` is the deployment's own code, and the previous changeset already states it awaits its send. The one in-repo relay, the shadowing `POST …/send-verification-email` route in `auth-plugin.ts` (`runResendVerificationEmail`), re-dispatches through `handleRequest` with a real `Request` carrying the caller's cookie and authorization headers, so a visitor through that door meets both halves of the rule; a visitor with an empty body is refused there before any re-dispatch (`email is required`). No door bypasses the rule.
6. **`Clause-②: no` (no arm) is true, and the plain `no` is the right declaration.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 is the rule text: "`Clause-②: yes|no` plus at most one arm from the closed pair `(widening)`/`(narrowing)` (`(narrowing)` is BREAKING, `no (widening)` malformed)". The reader's header (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, the authority on detail) states the question the value answers, 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」, and the arm's trigger: "A diff that NARROWS a published accept set answers it `no` truthfully — and a narrowing is a breaking change." The accept set of `POST /send-verification-email` is unchanged: the same body, the same callers, no export, schema or ledger entry moves (the new module is not re-exported; `index.ts` does not name it). What moves is the answer under a deployment condition the platform already names a refusal, through the one reader of that fact (`isEmailDeliveryLive`, which already decides the sign-up answer and the invite outcome, and which plugin-email answers `false` for its `log` transport in every environment). The template's own test for the narrowing face is whether the change "takes a declared capability away at the consumer, or makes the spec's own refusal real": a visitor's `200` on a `log` transport was a send to a log the visitor cannot read, and on an address with no account it was no send at all; the platform's refusal for that condition becomes real on one more door. Not a narrowing of a published accept set, so no `!`, no `(narrowing)` arm, no BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 marker, and no full dogfood battery owed (os-dev: the battery runs only on a `!` title or a `(narrowing)` arm). The judgment is close enough to record its one user-visible edge in ③.
7. **The pending changeset correction is right, and the edit stands.** `.changeset/sign-up-mail-after-response.md` line 12 listed the resend as unchanged; this PR keeps that true only for a signed-in caller, so the sentence now says so. Restoring the line from the merge base would republish a sentence this PR makes false, which is the one thing the gate's header says not to do. The new changeset `visitor-verification-resend.md` is `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth` with both declaration lines at line start; its prose matches the diff.
8. **§6 holds.** Title, body, both changesets and every test name state the rule (the same answer whatever the send does, whatever the address; one coded refusal while no transport is live). No advisory id, no attack wording, no mechanism narration beyond the rule; the one "probe" in the scan is pre-existing test-file prose on an unchanged line.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth` (released 18.3.0): `Metadata-protocol: none` is true (nothing an author writes changes), `Clause-②: no` with no arm is true per ① item 6, and a bug fix in a released package takes `patch`. The PR body and changeset lines parse at line start (the PR-body guards are green). Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev open question 1, the verify screens branching on the code: answered, not owed here.** `VerifyEmailPromptPage` already shows the server's `message`, and the refusal's message names the capability and the fix (Settings → Mail); the resend's `200` while a transport is live reads as sent, as the ruling orders. A code-keyed string in the console is a `ui/` follow-up at the seat's discretion, not a must-fix on this PR.
- **Dev open question 2, who confirms the changeset correction: the maintainer, in writing on this PR — escalated.** The gate's header calls it "the existing human path" and says staying red "puts the decision in front of a person"; the workflow step says the approver merges over the red. No seat confirms it. Until that written confirmation, the PR waits; the red is by design and blocks no required context.
- **Red-by-design condition still owed by the seat:** a PR comment naming `Check Changeset` and the DELIBERATE CORRECTION cause (SKILL.md: 源码自述、不跑 `merge_group`、PR 评论记明门与因). The first two hold on the tree and the workflow; the third needs the comment.
- **User-visible edge of the ruling, for the maintainer's awareness, not a defect:** the dev-default `log` transport is not live, so on a dev deployment a visitor's resend now reads the Settings → Mail refusal instead of writing the link to the log. That is what option G orders; it changes the dev loop for a visitor who has lost the sign-up log line.
- **Minor, not a must-fix:** while no transport is live, a signed-in caller whose session read throws in the before-hook is refused with the mail-configuration code rather than a read-fault status; the fallback is deliberate (a read that fails counts as no caller) and the condition is doubly degraded.
- The author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); no out-of-relay login to name.

### ④ Design judgment

- `visitor-verification-resend.ts` against the ruling and the code it cites: the rule is stated once, the two readers are placed where each can answer (the before-hook asks the actor reader every other before-hook gate uses; the callback asks the session the endpoint recorded), and the module's own fallback statement (the endpoint's reading decides how the send runs) is what makes the answer address-independent under any disagreement. Holds.
- `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts`: the rename widens the one wrapper from one path to two, keeping the awaited default for every other call; the comments scope the "throw so the resend is honest" rationale to the signed-in caller. Holds.
- `auth-manager-before-hook.ts`: one call, placed before the lockout gate, with `isEmailDeliveryLive` added to the host `Pick` alongside the existing members. Holds.
- Tests: ⑧ asks its three addresses concurrently against a deferred send and reads every answer before releasing it, which is the only honest way to pin "answered before the send settles"; the non-live battery covers the three ways a transport is not live; the signed-in case covers cookie and bearer, which is the exact seam the discriminator has. The scenario the PR is accepted against is covered.
